## TL;DR

The Work integration bar was being treated as a scrollable page shell. `#1130` moved
`<IntegrationStatusBar>` out of the desktop `.work-page` root (so phones keep the bar)
and made it a third root of WorkView's multi-root template. That put it directly under
`.main`, where the generic rule `.main > :not(.spin):not(.page-scroll):not(.work-page)…`
applies `overflow-y: auto` and `padding-bottom: var(--page-bottom-inset)` — 218px at the
default scale. On a `position: fixed; bottom: 74px` box, padding grows the box *upward*,
so the strip painted at the top of the padded content box, ~218px over the board.

I fixed it structurally: fixed overlays a view renders as `.main` children now carry a
`page-fixed-layer` marker that the page-inset rule excludes. The wrapper is once again a
pure positioning layer (zero padding, height == strip height), the strip hugs the bottom
nav on phones and sits 14px from the viewport bottom at ≥720px, and the expanded bar
grows upward from the same anchor. Geometry is now pinned by a real WebKit test at
360×740, 390×844, 412×915, 768×1024 and 1280×800, plus a single-task short-list case.

## Work and rationale

Reproduction came first. I built a WebKit fixture that loads the real `style.css` and the
real IntegrationStatusBar scoped CSS, with a `.main` containing a page shell, a tab bar,
and the actual `.ibar-wrap > .ibar-strip` markup. Before the fix it measured exactly the
reported numbers: at 390×844 the strip's bottom edge was 552 with the nav top at 781 and
`padding-bottom: 218px`; at 1280×800 the strip bottom was 568 in an 800px viewport. The
wrapper's box was 246px tall for a 28px strip. That confirmed the report's hypothesis
rather than the competing theories (stale `transform`, a drawer stacking context, or the
expanded bar's own height).

The regression is precisely the `#1130` template change. On `v0.5.87` the bar lived
inside `<div class="work-page">`, which the page-inset selector already excluded; it was
also `position: fixed`, so putting it there cost nothing. `#1130` split the two Work
compositions into mutually exclusive branches (`<template v-if="isNarrow">` versus the
desktop `.work-page`) and lifted the bar out so a phone would still show it. The
single-layout guarantee improved, but the bar's new parent made it subject to the page
padding rule.

The fix is one selector term plus one marker class, not an offset. In `style.css` the
page-inset rule now ends `:not(.inputs-board-page):not(.page-fixed-layer)` with a comment
explaining why fixed layers are not page shells. `WorkView.vue` renders
`<IntegrationStatusBar class="ibar-outer page-fixed-layer" />`. Nothing else in the bar
component changed: its mobile block (`bottom: calc(74px + var(--safe-bot))`) and desktop
block (`bottom: 14px`) were already correct, and the desktop centering transform still
works because the padding that used to inflate the box is gone.

Content clearance was already handled by the existing owners, so I deliberately left it
alone: the phone queue's routed root keeps `--page-bottom-inset` on its scrollport (which
comfortably clears a bar topping out ~104px above the viewport bottom), `MobileTaskDetail`
adds its own inset, and the desktop board columns keep `.col-body::after` with
`flex: 0 0 var(--page-bottom-inset)`. The `.ibar-spacer` in WorkView stays as-is
(`display: none` on the desktop board).

## Approaches tried

- **Negative offset / compensating bottom**: rejected outright. It would have hidden the
  symptom while leaving a scrollable, padded fixed wrapper that still wasted ~218px of
  hit area and would break again on any inset change.
- **Move the bar to `App.vue` next to `FloatingHeads`**: rejected for scope. It changes
  where the bar renders (every route, or route-gated by hand), and the bar is Work's
  ambient pipeline status by design.
- **Single WorkView root wrapper**: rejected because the two layouts own scrolling very
  differently (`.work-page` is a height-owning flex column; the phone queue is the page
  scroller). A shared wrapper would have to be excluded from the same rule anyway, or it
  would introduce a new scrollport and change the phone queue's scroll owner.
- **Teleport the bar to `<body>`**: plausible but larger. It changes stacking relative to
  the drawer and `MobileTabs`, and the bar is already correctly fixed; only its box was
  wrong.
- **Chosen: an explicit opt-out marker on the fixed layer.** It names the concept
  ("a fixed layer is not a page"), applies to any future overlay, and is asserted both
  statically and by real geometry.

While tracing the selector I checked every other `position: fixed` descendant of `.main`
and every other `.main > …` rule. WorkView is the only view that renders a fixed child as
a direct `.main` sibling; the app-level overlays (drawer, tab bar, floating heads, toasts)
live outside `.main`. So this is the whole class, not one instance.

## Challenges and blockers

- The repo's vitest entry point needs `src/ui-app/vite.config.ts` for `.vue` imports; a
  bare `bunx vitest run` fails to parse SFCs. I used `bun run test:vitest <paths>`.
- Playwright's WebKit binary is present in this environment, so the geometry suite ran
  rather than skipping.
- `repoos check --changed main` passed, but the environment sets `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`
  (the suite is delegated to the remote validation runner), so the new tests were
  verified by running them directly: 150 passing across the four affected UI test files,
  including 104 in the WebKit page-height suite.

## Key learnings

- Page padding applied to a `position: fixed` element is not cosmetic: with `auto`
  height and a bottom anchor it enlarges the box upward and detaches the content from the
  bottom. Any fixed overlay that becomes a `.main` child needs the marker.
- Multi-root view templates in Vue make every root a `.main` sibling; structural
  assumptions that held for a single-root page (insets, flex fill, overflow) apply to each
  root separately.
- Measuring before and after in the same WebKit fixture is what turned a plausible
  hypothesis into a proven one, and it gave the regression test real numbers instead of
  guessed ones.
